newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post fourth straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post fourth straight record close.

text.p: Toronto stocks posted their fourth straight record close on Thursday, boosted by a rally in heavyweight energy stocks.
The Toronto Stock Exchange 300 Composite Index gained 26.73 points to 6877.30, its 31st record close of 1997.

The oil and gas sector, which makes up almost 14 percent of the index, rose two percent after Suncor Energy Inc. unveiled a plan to invest C$2.2 billion ($1.6 billion) in its Canadian oil sands business to boost synthetic oil output.
Investors have flocked to equity markets due to the lack of investment alternatives, especially with bond interest rates dropping, said Rolie Bradley of Maison Placements Canada.
"The lower the interest rates go...the more the propensity for people to buy more stock," Bradley said.
Trading was brisk on Thursday with volume of 114 million shares worth C$2 billion ($1.4 billion).
Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were evenly divided with gaining sectors led by oils, transportation and pipelines.
The weak side included conglomerates, consumer products and media.
Advancing issues beat decliners 579 to 439, with 273 ending flat.
Shares in Suncor, Canada's fourth largest integrated oil firm, jumped 7.20, or almost 19 percent, to 45.65 in active trading.
High technology firm JDS FITEL Inc. rallied 7.50, or more than 16 percent, to close at 53.
JDS, a component maker for the fiber-optic communications industry, reported sharply higher fourth-quarter earnings.

International investment firm Global Equity Corp. slipped 0.09 to 2.59 on 7.39 million shares following news that PICO Holdings Inc. acquired an additional 6.6 million shares of Global Equity from Mackenzie Financial Corp. at C$2.38 ($1.70) a share.
